clue.text: Female is behind fashionable leading product

parts.note: lags means trails or is behind
hip means trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: A woman's company has fallen behind with its trendy best-selling item.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's flagship is its best or most important product, the one that leads its range.

clue.text: Noted obsession engaging the writer

indicators.note: engaging means the word for obsession holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a fad is a short-lived craze or obsession
the writer means the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A well-known craze has captured the author.
explanation.definitionFit: Famed means celebrated or well known, so noted.

clue.text: A lad's misbehaving with girl in dances

indicators.note: misbehaving means the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: the 's here is the plural, giving the letters of lads

explanation.surface: A boy is behaving badly with a girl on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges A LADS together with GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Galliards are lively sixteenth-century court dances in triple time.

clue.text: Brave woman given drug when having minimal energy

parts.note: heroin is an opiate drug

indicators.note: minimal means only the smallest part, the first letter, of energy is used

explanation.surface: A courageous woman is given drugs when she is exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is a woman admired for courage or noble deeds.

clue.text: I couldn't rush up — I must be composed, beautiful

indicators.note: must be composed means the letters are to be arranged, made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone vain insists on calm before showing off their good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'I couldn't rush up' plus the second 'I'; 'must be composed' rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulchritudinous is a grand word meaning physically beautiful, from Latin pulcher, beautiful.

clue.text: Legendary association of sportsmen exploited extortionately

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, which governs the sport in England
to bleed someone is to drain them of money, so bled means fleeced

explanation.surface: A famous sporting body has been squeezing its supporters for every penny.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA (Football Association) runs English football; 'bled' is the sense of extracting money ruthlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fabled is told of in stories and myths, so it is legendary.

clue.text: Get rid of nasty person's hot supporting piece?

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them
a dog is slang for a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Sack a horrible person's hot backer?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: the piece supports burning logs.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog, or andiron, is a metal stand that supports logs in a fireplace, so it gets very hot.

clue.text: Port? Litres English possess right for drinking

indicators.note: for drinking means the word for possess takes the next letter into itself

parts.note: to have is to possess

explanation.surface: Litres of port that the English have the right to drink?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port?' looks like the fortified wine, fitting 'litres' and 'drinking', but it is a harbour town; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major French seaport at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: Writer protected by editor when in depression, as a hanger-on

indicators.note: in places the whole assembled piece inside the word for depression

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression

indicators.note: protected by means the writer sits inside the abbreviation for editor

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer sheltered by an editor while feeling low is just a sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' and 'in' nest the pieces two deep, making EPEND before it goes into the hollow; 'depression' suggests low spirits but is a dip in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependent is a person who relies on another for support, such as a hanger-on.

clue.text: Fruit tree gets one fussing audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the word for one fussing is only heard, not spelt, here

parts.note: a meddler is a busybody who fusses and interferes

explanation.surface: An orchard tree attracts a busybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The medlar is a small tree of the rose family grown for its brown fruit, eaten when half rotten.

clue.text: Address for a man in a superior Westminster house

definitions.text: Address for a man in a superior Westminster house

parts.words: Address for a man in a superior Westminster house
parts.note: the upper chamber at Westminster is the House of Lords, and a male peer there is addressed with this title

explanation.surface: How to speak to a gentleman in a grand house in Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'superior' house is the upper house of Parliament, the House of Lords; a peer is addressed as 'Your ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title used when speaking to or of a peer, as in 'his ...' or 'your ...', is the form of address for a lord.

clue.text: Unreported evil is horrible — what's covered up is very bad

indicators.note: what is covered up among the preceding words is a run of letters concealed across them

explanation.surface: A wicked deed nobody reported is dreadful, and the cover-up is worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the D at the end of 'Unreported' through 'evil is' to the H of 'horrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish means fiendishly wicked or extremely bad, as bad as the devil himself.

clue.text: Daughter torn apart, being highly motivated?

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees
riven means split or torn apart

explanation.surface: A daughter is heartbroken and yet fiercely ambitious?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone driven is highly motivated, pushed on by ambition; the clue's 'being' turns the adjective into the state.

clue.text: PM finds Irish deal not hard surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters come out in an unexpected new order
not means the letter for hard is left out of the word Irish

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister arrives at an Irish agreement that is unexpectedly gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H from IRISH to leave IRIS; with DEAL, 'surprisingly' rearranges IRISDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British Prime Minister, so he is a PM.

clue.text: Ladies used to get excited about indoor game

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters are placed around the game
to get excited means the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: chess is a board game played indoors

explanation.surface: Women who once became animated over a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get excited' rearranges USED into DUES, which goes 'about' CHESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesses are noblewomen, wives of dukes, and so ladies of rank.

clue.text: Go perhaps to the empty cell

parts.note: Go is an Asian board game, so it is an example of a game

indicators.note: empty means the word the loses its middle, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to go to the cell that has been vacated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go perhaps' looks like a command but is the board game Go, an example of a GAME; 'empty' turns THE into TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, an egg or sperm, that fuses with another in fertilisation.

clue.text: Alice's companion gets to walk, then run

parts.note: to march is to walk briskly in step
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Alice's friend gets to stroll, then sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: The March Hare is the character who hosts the mad tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: Pet starts to sleep, soundly ensconced in bed

indicators.note: in puts the opening letters inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed, typically for a baby

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A pet animal settles down for a good sleep tucked into its bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes S, S and E from 'sleep, soundly, ensconced', and 'in' places them inside COT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone in the sense of pampering them is to cosset, indulge or fuss over them.

clue.text: Group needing trade show to be settled

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
a fair is an exhibition of goods, a trade show

explanation.surface: A group needs a trade exhibition to settle things.
explanation.walkthrough: SET FAIR is the barometer marking for steady fine weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair describes weather that is fine and settled, as marked on barometers.

clue.text: Vessel in army vehicle stuck on a road

indicators.note: stuck on means the following pieces are attached after the vehicle

parts.note: a tank is an armoured military vehicle

explanation.surface: A ship's container is inside a military vehicle that is stuck on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, often pewter with a handle, a type of drinking vessel.

clue.text: As a business person try to outmanoeuvre strike

definitions.text: As a business person try to outmanoeuvre
definitions.meaning: a trader beats rivals by selling for less than they do
in boxing a punch delivered upwards from below

explanation.definitionFit: To undercut is both to offer goods cheaper than a competitor and to hit with an upward blow.

clue.text: One who may help guest Norma, drunk after party

indicators.note: after means the party comes first, followed by the next piece

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of the name stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: After a party Norma was drunk and needed a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman at a hotel or club opens doors and assists guests as they arrive and leave.

clue.text: Yesteryear's lover, flighty type who is non-resident?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, a lover from the past
a tern is a seabird, a creature that flies

explanation.surface: A former sweetheart who is a fickle sort no longer lives here?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' looks like fickle but here means given to flight: the seabird TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: An extern is a student or medical worker who lives outside the institution, so is not resident there.

clue.text: Weather line on map — one thus gets temperature on island

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
so means thus or in this way
Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands, near Guernsey

explanation.surface: A forecaster's line on the chart shows the heat on a particular island.
explanation.walkthrough: HERM is a small Channel Island off Guernsey, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a line on a weather map joining places of equal temperature.

clue.text: Possibly a yen to be held in honour

indicators.note: to be held in means the following letters sit inside the honour

parts.note: the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency yen

explanation.surface: Perhaps a desire to be honoured by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like a longing but is the Japanese currency, Y. The MBE is a British honour given for service.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and possibly both mean perhaps, expressing uncertainty.

clue.text: Two cats so out of sorts, not running smoothly

indicators.note: out of sorts means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: two cats gives the word cat once
and the word cat a second time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of moody felines are jerky in their movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two cats' is not fodder as written: it gives CAT twice; with SO, 'out of sorts' rearranges CATCATSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato describes notes or speech that are short and detached, the opposite of a smooth legato flow.

clue.text: Despicably virile having injected drug

indicators.note: having injected means the drug goes inside the word for virile

parts.note: manly means virile or masculine
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A macho man shamefully took drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To act meanly is to behave in a petty, contemptible way, so despicably.

clue.text: Hospital for brief time in Glos. town able to provide shelter

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another in the town's name

parts.note: Stroud is a market town in Gloucestershire, an English county
T is the short form of time
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital in a Gloucestershire town can give refuge to people for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: Glos. is short for Gloucestershire, a county in western England; STROUD is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: A shroud is a covering that screens or protects, so something capable of giving cover.

clue.text: One has a subject offering judgement

definitions.meaning: a grammatical unit of words that contains a subject and a verb
the punishment a court pronounces on a convicted criminal

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a complete grammatical statement with subject and verb, and a court's punishment.
